findings.title: Harvest count and harvested weight are multiplied by the number of journal entries
findings.where: GET /api/plants, GET /api/plants/{id}; Plants list, plant detail, delete-plant confirmation
findings.steps: Tomato has 3 harvests (600+450+300 g) and 2 journal entries. Open /plants or GET /api/plants.
findings.actual: Tomato: harvest_count 6, harvest_grams 2700 (shown as 2.7 kg). Adding a journal entry to any plant with harvests inflates its harvest totals again.
findings.evidence: GET /api/harvests lists plant 1 weights 600,450,300, but GET /api/plants returns harvest_count=6, harvest_grams=2700, journal_count=2. PLANT_SELECT adds LEFT JOIN journal_entries, but COUNT(h.id) and SUM(h.weight_grams) are not de-duplicated (only the journal count uses DISTINCT).

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout: hung add/search spins forever
findings.where: Plant detail 'Add entry'; Journal page search
findings.steps: Make POST /api/journal hang (no response), type an entry and click Add entry, then wait over 10 s. Or on /journal make GET /api/journal hang and type a search.
findings.expected: Fails after 10 s with a visible error; the button becomes usable again
findings.actual: The button shows 'Saving…' and stays disabled indefinitely. The Journal page shows 'Loading entries…' indefinitely, with the previous search's results still listed under the new search term.
findings.evidence: After 12 s: 'Saving…' still shown; Journal page after 12 s for q=zzz: 'Loading entries…' plus the stale Lettuce result. useApiClient/useApiFetch set no timeout.

findings.title: Journal load errors have no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal return 500, then open a plant or the Journal page through in-app links.
findings.expected: Error message with a Retry button that reloads the data when the server is back
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, with no retry control. On the plant page the only way to recover is a reload, or adding or deleting an entry.
findings.evidence: Error text shown; count of buttons named retry/try again = 0 on both pages.

findings.title: Unreadable (non-list) journal response is shown as an empty journal
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal return 200 with {"items":[]} (any non-array), then navigate to Journal in the app.
findings.actual: Shows '0 entries' and 'No journal entries yet'
findings.evidence: Page text: '0 entries / No journal entries yet / Open a plant and write the first entry...'

findings.title: Null fields render as 'null journal entries' or a bare dash
findings.steps: Mock GET /api/plants with journal_count null, or GET /api/journal with plant_name/body/entry_on null, then navigate in the app.
findings.expected: A sensible fallback or an error
findings.actual: Plants card shows 'null journal entries'; the journal feed item shows an empty plant link and body, with only '–' for the date.
findings.evidence: Page text 'null journal entries'; journal feed '1 entry\n\n–'

findings.title: Oversized ids give 500 instead of 4xx on journal endpoints
Retrying an add after a timeout or lost response creates duplicate entries
findings.steps: Submit an entry whose response is lost or slow, then click Add entry again once the button is usable
findings.actual: There is no idempotency key or de-duplication, so each retry inserts a new row. In testing, a POST that was held while the route was blocked was still delivered later and created 'Hang test entry', while the UI never confirmed it.
findings.evidence: 'Hang test entry' appeared in the Courgette journal although the UI never confirmed that save.

findings.title: Search over 80 characters shows a raw validation error
findings.steps: Type or paste 81+ characters into Search
findings.expected: Input limited, or a friendly message
findings.actual: The API returns 422 (q max_length 80) and the page swaps the results for 'Q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The input has no maxlength.

findings.title: The 'today' rule uses different clocks on client and server
findings.steps: Use a browser whose time zone is ahead of the server's (e.g. UTC+13) just after local midnight, and add an entry dated today
findings.actual: The client allows today's date (browser time zone), but the server's date.today() still sees yesterday and rejects it as 'Journal date cannot be in the future.'
findings.evidence: Code: todayIso() uses the browser's local date; the validator uses the server's local date.
